metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Hommel's method (1988) is slightly more complicated, but it is more powerful than the Simes-Hochberg correction (Hommel 1989). Under Hommel's method, we reject all hypotheses whose p values are less than or equal to $ \pi/k^{*} $, where $$ k^{*}=\max_{i}\left(p(n-i+j)>\pi\frac{j}{i}\right)\quad for all j=1,\cdots,i $$
